newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares weighed down by profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares weighed down by profit taking.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 0.26 percent on Monday as investors continued to cash in profits ahead of a new securities tax coming into force on January 1.
The 10-share SBI index fell 2.99 points to 1,160.0, down 0.7 percent from last Monday.
"Today and tommorow are the last days for those who want to sell ahead of the new tax so tommorow's situation may look similar," Davor Dubokovic, a trader of Eastbrokers said.
He expects trading on the Ljubljana bourse to pick up again in the first half of next year on expectations of stepped-up participation from foreigners.
"We expect positive changes on the market next year as shares of some very good newly privatised companies will be listed and that will probably attract many new foreign investors," Dubokovic added
Turnover surged to 226.8 million tolars from 87.3 million tolars. Overall five shares fell, 10 rose and five were unchanged, while five were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 0.29 percent to 41,750 tolars on volume of 2,872 shares.
Bank SKB last month announced plans to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange early next year. SKB would be the first Slovenian company to get a foreign listing.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the day's leading decliner, tumbling 18.84 percent closing at 21,500 tolars on volume of 35 shares.
Slovenia's only port Luka Koper was the biggest gainer, firming 3.83 percent to close at 1,950 tolars on volume of 1,771 shares.
